code: size_t CAPSTONE_API cs_disasm(csh ud, const uint8_t *buffer, size_t size, uint64_t offset, size_t count, cs_insn **insn)
note: The fuzzer-controlled instruction bytes are passed into the Capstone disassembler as buffer and drive X86 instruction decoding.

code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
note: The architecture decoder consumes the input bytes and stores the decoded internal X86 opcode in mci.Opcode.

code: unsigned int i = find_insn(insns, ARR_SIZE(insns), id);
note: The decoded internal opcode must have a public mapping; when find_insn returns -1 the function leaves insn->id unset instead of assigning a safe invalid id.
The unset public instruction id remains in the cs_insn object returned to the caller.
The fuzz target reads the uninitialized public instruction id and passes it to cs_insn_name.
X86_insn_name branches on the uninitialized id value, producing the MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value report.
